page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core, backed by the Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, but offers a high baseline network bandwidth of 67 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the c8gb.8xlarge demonstrates top-tier memory performance, achieving a Passmark memory score and large-block read/write bandwidths in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core capabilities are also highly competitive, with Geekbench multi-core scores reaching the top 10% tier. Database operations and Redis SET operations show strong performance, alongside high static web serving throughput and efficient software compilation. However, single-core performance and LLM inference speeds, particularly text generation on smaller models and prompt processing on larger models, fall into the average to weak categories.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture delivers high resource density and exceptional memory bandwidth per core, making it highly efficient for multi-threaded workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. Given the lack of local storage and GPU accelerators, this server is best suited for network-heavy, compute-intensive workloads such as high-throughput web serving, database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded data decompression.
